## P1 — Metrics are not comparable; no preferred candidate is currently supportable

| Subject | Reported authoring LOC | Generic glue LOC | Files/module | Binding loci |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| A/B1 | 19 | 17 | 1 | 1 |
| B/B2-L | 14 | 4 | 1 | 1 |

These numbers use different inputs and counting boundaries. B itself has two incompatible implementations. Some counts include scenario tables, some count only a declaration, and C separates activation while A/B do not. Consequently even an arithmetically calculated glue ratio would compare unlike denominators.

Also absent on a shared basis are compile-time samples, diagnostic/error-quality scoring, `.d.ts` snapshots, serializability, hostile-key behavior, deletion/disable cost, 10/100/1000-module measurements, runtime import counts, Pure DI parity, and tree-shaking evidence.

Therefore:

- No evidence-backed preferred A/B/C candidate can be selected today.
- A later preference may be explicitly private and qualification-only without creating a public API. Current authority permits private qualification names while public naming remains gated: [current-contract.md](/var/data/gm-goal-audit-20260904/workspaces/api/docs/architecture/current-contract.md:31).
- Any B-like helper must respect the already accepted exact behavior—`required()`, `optional()`, `many({min,max})`, and identity-preserving `defineModule(x)`—rather than copying the present B variants: [ADR-0007](/var/data/gm-goal-audit-20260904/workspaces/api/docs/decisions/0007-require-executable-v1-conformance-amendments.md:427).
- C’s declaration/activation separation may remain a product-host adapter seam, but it is not currently proven as the preferred Core authoring candidate.

### Minimal qualification-only closure

Suggested structure:

```text
tests/qualification/implementation-readiness/api-authoring/shared/
  adapter.ts
  corpus.ts
  oracle.ts
tests/qualification/implementation-readiness/api-authoring/candidates/
  a-descriptor.ts
  b-define-module.ts
  c-declaration-activation.ts
tests/qualification/implementation-readiness/api-authoring/tests/
  corpus-identity.test.ts
  runtime.test.ts
  types.test.ts
  loader-and-di.test.ts
  type-scale.mjs
  measure.mjs
tests/qualification/implementation-readiness/api-authoring/expected/
  a.d.ts
  b.d.ts
  c.d.ts
tests/qualification/implementation-readiness/api-authoring/results/
  scenarios.json
  metrics.json
tsconfig.json
README.md
```

Design:

- `corpus.ts`: one frozen, plain-data definition of exactly the numbered 30 cases and expected canonical outcomes.
- `adapter.ts`: one qualification interface receiving the same scenario object and returning inert declaration/profile data plus a separately held host construction function.
- Candidate adapters only encode/decode their syntax. They must not implement different defaults or scenario semantics.
- `oracle.ts`: a small disposable deterministic evaluator owned entirely by qualification; no imports from production Core.
- C keeps factories outside declarations. Literal loaders live only in the host test and are selected from an in-memory literal table.
- Scenario 28 compares closed dependency-record construction with direct handwritten Pure DI—no resolver, registry, or container.

Tests and outputs:

- Assert exactly 30 unique IDs, one corpus digest, and 90 candidate executions.
- Execute exact diagnostics/outcomes, hostile keys, permutation stability, JSON/structured-clone safety, hidden-fallback rejection, selected-loader counters, and direct-DI parity.
- Run positive and negative TypeScript cases and retain readable `.d.ts` snapshots.
- Generate 10/100/1000-module sources in an OS-temporary directory and record identical-run median/range compile times.
- `scenarios.json`: corpus digest, per-candidate result, exact diagnostic code/path, serialized-output digest, and import counters.
- `metrics.json`: authoring/glue LOC with explicit denominators, ratio, files, binding loci, explicit annotations, `.d.ts` lines/bytes/exports, TypeScript diagnostics, compile timings, inventory digest, serialization bytes, removal/disable edits, and tree-shaking as either measured with an already pinned tool or `not-measured` with reason.
- Approximate total: 750–850 non-generated LOC—about 180 corpus, 100 oracle, 130 adapters, 250 tests/measurement, and 90 types/config/readme.

Stop conditions:

- Stop without a winner if any of the 90 cells is missing, name-only, hard-coded from expected output, or uses a different corpus digest.
- Stop if an adapter changes semantics, supplies a hidden default/fallback, or embeds executable values in declarations.
- Stop on any production-Core import/change, framework/container, decorator/reflection, filesystem discovery, registration-order behavior, or accepted-ADR edit.
- Stop if metric definitions, compiler settings, toolchain, or sample sizes differ by candidate.
- Stop before public exports, package/barrel selection, or claiming a public API. A winner may only be labeled a disposable private qualification preference.
